articles.summary: WWE News: Explore the financial legacies of Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair in 2026. Discover their net worth, WWE earnings, UFC careers, endorsements, and lifestyle differences.
articles.body: Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE. Their current net-worth estimates vary significantly across sources and should be treated cautiously because personal assets, debts, taxes, expenses and private income are not fully disclosed.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair net worth in 2026Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number. The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Financial categoryBrock LesnarRic FlairEstimated net worth, 2026$10M–$20M$500K–$5M*Primary careerWWE, UFC, amateur wrestlingProfessional wrestlingMajor promotionWWEWCW, WWEUFC achievementFormer UFC Heavyweight ChampionN/AMain modern incomeWrestling, appearances, endorsementsAppearances, licensing, wrestling-related workLesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Brock Lesnar’s WWE career earnings and wealthLesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s wrestling career earnings and financial journeyRic Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.How Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair continue building their fortunesLesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. articles.title: AEW Full Gear 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of AEW Full Gear 2026 from Phoenix Arizona.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of AEW Full Gear 2026 from Phoenix Arizona.

This year's event is serving as a bit of an unofficial tribute show for Pac due to the name of the show being born from a joke made during a BTE segment.

As usual, AEW packed the card with title bouts, stipulations, grudge matches and all of the major players currently in storylines.

Let's take a look at what went down at this year's show.

Here is the lineup from this year's Full Gear PPV.

Queen Aminata vs. Persephone vs. Hyan vs. Skye Blue (TBS Championship)

The Brawling Birds vs. Wrathlander (Women's Tag Team Championships)

The Young Bucks vs. Mark Davis and Jake Doyle (Men's Tag Team Championships)

Brodido and Adam Page vs. The New Level and Swerve Strickland (Trios Championships)

The Death Riders vs. The Cut (Anarchy in the Arena)

Kazuchika Okada vs. Adam Copeland (International Championship)

Tommaso Ciampa vs. Ilja Dragunov (National Championship)

Marina Shafir vs. Mercedes Mone (Women's World Championship)

Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher (AEW World Heavyweight Championship)

The first match on the pre-show saw Jack Perry Battle The Beast Mortos. There was no real story behind this match, so it was just two guys fighting to get a win at a major event, and sometimes that is all you need.

This was a solid match. It was good, but not in a way that is going to outshine what is set to come, so it was a nice way to get the crowd into the right mood without the show peaking too early. Perry sent a message to Samoa Joe by hitting Mortos with a Muscle Buster to get the win.

Wardlow, Kevin Knight and El Clon vs. Local Talents

Three members of the Don Callis Family were in action against three local talents. As you could probably assume from that description, this was not a very long fight.

Each member of the DCF had a chance to be in the ring for a few moments to hit some moves. It was over within a couple of minutes, with Knight scoring the pin for his team.

The next match kept the DCF at ringside with Rocky Romero, Trent Beretta, Lance Archer and Josh Alexander taking on Darius Martin, Matt Sydal, QT Marshall and Big Boom AJ, the Costco guy.

This was a little more exciting than the usual Costco Guys match, but it was still kind of gimmicky and felt like a random excuse to throw a bunch of people together. Boom and Doom continued to be undefeated after getting the win.

Result: Boom and Doom, Martin and Sydal won

Queen Aminata vs. Persephone vs. Hyan vs. Skye Blue

The only match on the pre-show that really mattered ended the Tailgate Brawl with Aminata defending her TBS title against Persephone, Hyan and Skye Blue. The original plan was a triple threat with Maya World, but travel issues forced a change to the card.

This was high-energy right out of the gate. All four women were giving it their all and delivered a fun performance. This easily outshone everything else on the pre-show. Aminata was able to get the win to retain her title.

Before the show, AEW revealed that the trios titles now contain a tribute to Pac on the leather straps.

Perry has added a little bit of size to his physique. It's not much, but enough to be visibly noticeable.

One of the jobbers had some trouble getting up for the powerbomb.

The Rizzler and Big Justice were not at ringside.

The way Blue took a chair to the face looked brutal.

Kazuchika Okada vs. Adam Copeland (International Title)

The first match on the main card saw Copeland challenge Okada for the International Championship. This is one of those matches that seemed impossible for a long time, so a lot of fans were excited to see two veterans have their first singles match ever.

The Rainmaker was the first to get the upper hand after playing his usual mind games, but Cope did not let him keep it for long. He made Okada leave the ring to take a breather after almost hitting a Spear very early.

The champion exposed part of the concrete floor and attempted a piledriver, but he was unsuccessful. It ended up coming back into play later when Okada hit an Impaler on the floor.

This match had a steady pace and was structured more in sequences than as one continuous fight. They would pick up the pace, hit a big move, and then slow down again for a bit. It's a tried-and-true formula that many matches have used.

Okada and Copeland had very different careers leading to this point, and have worked in very different styles, but being the pros that they are, they had zero issues finding their groove and giving us a fun show.

The Rated-R Superstar put up a good fight, but The Rainmaker got the win to retain his title.

Okada's entrance gear was a little more ornate than usual.

Cope hit an atomic drop onto a steel chair. It did not look like it would be very painful, but Okada sold it well.

There were some very anti-Don Callis fans near the ring.

Okada received a small cut on his arm after being sent into the ring post, but it did not bleed much.

The Young Bucks vs. Davis and Doyle (Men's Tag Team Titles)

Nick and Matt Jackson put their tag titles on the line against the two men who absolutely destroyed them in their last meeting, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle.

Much like in their previous encounter, the two powerhouses took control immediately. They brought the Bucks out of the ring and punished them against various parts of the set, and it looked like they might get a squash win again.

Unfortunately for the DCF, the Bucks put up more of a fight this time. Davis and Doyle still felt dominant, especially in the early minutes, but it wasn't quite as one-sided as it was last time.

Seeing Davis and Doyle finally being portrayed as a dominant force has been fantastic to watch. They feel unique in the landscape of AEW while simultaneously feeling like a throwback to tag teams of the past.

Once the Bucks started to mount some real offense, things really picked up. Their high-flying style was the perfect contrast to the powerhouse style used by their opponents, so there was a nice variety of offense throughout the match.

This match exceeded all expectations, and people were already expecting it to be good. The only thing that would have made this better was a title change, but the Bucks retained after a stellar performance from all four competitors.

The Motor City Machine Guns came out after the match since they are next in line for a title shot. They helped the Bucks up and hugged them before helping them celebrate their win, and that is when The Kasper Brothers, formerly known as The Creeds in WWE, made their debut.

They attacked and took out all four men before FTR came out. It looked like they might fight the newcomers, but they ended up joining forces, so it looks like Stokely Hathaway has some new clients that he used to manage in The Diamond Mine in NXT.

Result: The Young Bucks defeated Davis and Doyle

Unlike during Okada vs. Cope, Don Callis joined the commentary team for this one.

If you watched mid-90s WCW, Davis and Doyle are giving big Men at Work vibes, and we mean that as a compliment.

The way Nick helped Matt get Davis into position for the Meltzer Driver was creative.

The bump Nick took on the timekeeper's table looked nasty.

articles.title: Stephen Thompson Reflects On Retirement Before Last UFC Fight
articles.summary: Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson talks about what led him to call it a career ahead of his final UFC fight against Charles Radtke.
articles.body:
10-year UFC veteran Stephen Thompson is calling it a career after his fight with Charles Radtke at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden.

After a historic run in the promotion, the 43-year-old Wonderboy will step into the Octagon for a final time against a young competitor. When asked what brought him to the decision, Thompson told Forbes that recovery started getting difficult with age. Additionally, the birth of his daughter urged him to step away from MMA.

"My body does not recover like it used to," Thompson shared. "After my last fight, I went back to training and jacked my neck up; I hurt my lower back, and my knee started hurting. I had to slow down, back off on the hard training, and my body started to feel better."

"I realized I don't have a lot of time to be in the UFC, competing against these young studs. But not only that, I have a baby girl; she's five months, and that definitely changes your mindset as well," he added.

"I wanna have my body nice and healthy; five, ten, fifteen years from now, we can go hiking, riding bikes, and I won't be too banged up. That does change your mind, but when your body knows, it's time."

The kickboxing savant made his professional MMA debut at 26 after a successful amateur career.

Following a 5-0 start, Wonderboy joined the UFC in 2012. He went on to win eight of his nine fights, including four knockouts, in the promotion before a stalemate with Tyron Woodley in his first title challenge. The pair met again, but the decision favored Woodley in the rematch.

Thompson has since been 4-7 and heads into UFC 334 on a three-fight skid despite wins against impressive competition in Jorge Masvidal, Vicente Luque, and Kevin Holland. His three latest defeats came at the hands of top fighters in Gabriel Bonfim, Joaquin Buckley, and Shavkat Rakhmonov.

With the likes of Amanda Nunes, Henry Cejudo and Georges St-Pierre returning from initial retirements, Thompson is not closing the door to competing in other disciplines.

"My competitive itch is still there, but I think I'm done with MMA," he said. "I'm a striker at heart, so maybe I'll do some boxing in the future. But we'll see what that holds when she gets a little older."

"Your body knows when it's done, and you gotta accept it. You sit down with your coaches and family. I'm very close with my training partners, and I thought it's time. It was heartbreaking, and I don't know what emotions are gonna be on fight night. I may start bawling, but my main focus is getting ready."

Facing Thompson on his swansong is 36-year-old Charles Radtke, who is riding a two-fight win streak. The 12-5 fighter joined the UFC in 2023 and is 5-2 in the promotion.

When asked about his opponent, Wonderboy raved about the type of fight Radtke presents.

"He's coming at you," he said. "That's what made me want this fight. He's a battle-worn guy; he likes to put on a show, good boxing, good takedowns. I'm ready wherever the fight goes. He brings it, and that's the kind of show we want to put on at Madison Square Garden."

Wonderboy is no stranger to the bright lights at the World's Most Famous Arena. After the draw with Woodley, Thompson fought twice more at the Garden, tallying wins over Masvidal and Luque.

"Having spent some time in the Empire State, Thompson marveled at the chance to end his career with another win at Madison Square Garden."

"It's epic. To be able to go out there, New York is my home away from home," he shared. "I spent a lot of time on Long Island with Chris Weidman, Matt Serra and Ray Longo, and I fought here four times. This is my jam."

"To be able to go out with a dub for my fans here in MSG in New York City would be epic."

Apart from his entertaining fight style, Wonderboy became beloved by fans for being one of the kindest people in a dangerous sport. A victory on Saturday would elevate him to a 17-9-1 record before laying the gloves down.

"I wanna be remembered as one of the best strikers to step out in the Octagon," Thompson shared. "One of the best martial artists and just a good dude. Just a kind guy. You don't have to have a crazy persona to make it in the UFC. Being yourself is sometimes the best route and is a breath of fresh air."

articles.title: Kasper Brothers Make AEW Debut After WWE Exit, Attack Young Bucks in Viral Video at Full Gear
articles.summary: The Kasper Brothers are officially All Elite.
articles.body:
The Kasper Brothers are officially All Elite.

After the Young Bucks beat Mark Davis and Jake Doyle at Full Gear on Saturday to retain the AEW World Tag Team Championships, the Kasper Brothers arrived for their AEW debut.

As the Young Bucks stood tall in the ring following their win, the Kasper Brothers arrived and attacked them in a shocking appearance that comes not long after they exited WWE following the expiration of their contracts.

The Kasper Brothers (Jacob and Drew Kasper), known as the Creed Brothers in WWE, exited the company earlier this month after six years following the expiration of their contracts.

Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp reported on Nov. 6 that their exit "appears to be a mutual parting of ways."

The pair had been a staple on WWE NXT, most recently competing in the 2026 Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic in September. Their final match was a loss to Hank & Tank in the quarterfinals of the tournament in October.

So now the Kasper Brothers move to AEW, where they are clearly hoping to get a piece of the Young Bucks and perhaps challenge them for the AEW Tag Team Title in the future.

As for Saturday's match, Davis and Doyle earned a title opportunity in shocking fashion, as they defeated The Young Bucks in a title eliminator match on the Oct. 21 episode of Dynamite.

Beating The Bucks in any manner would have been a huge deal, but Davis and Doyle decimated Nick and Matt Jackson in a matter of only a few minutes, making it even more impressive.

Just a few days earlier, The Young Bucks defended the AEW World Tag Team Championships against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight at WrestleDream in a match that clearly took a lot out of them.

Davis and Doyle took advantage of the situation and benefited from the damage their Don Callis Family stablemates had done to The Bucks.

As impactful as that victory was in terms of earning them a title opportunity at Full Gear, Davis and Doyle took it a step further a couple of weeks later.

On the Nov. 4 edition of Dynamite, Davis and Doyle were part of The Don Callis Family's team in Blood & Guts, and they defeated a team that included The Young Bucks.

That gave Davis and Doyle two meaningful victories over Nick and Matt Jackson over the course of a few weeks, securing them all the momentum they could ask for ahead of Full Gear.

Despite that, The Young Bucks rose to the occasion and retained their titles, ensuring their continued reign over a hugely competitive tag team division.

articles.title: New Level vs. Hangman Page, Brodido AEW Trios Title Match Winner, Top Highlights from Full Gear 2026
articles.summary: Swerve Strickland and The New Level beat "Hangman" Adam Page and Brodido in a Texas Deathmatch at Full Gear on Saturday to win the AEW World Trios Championships.
articles.body:
Swerve Strickland and The New Level beat "Hangman" Adam Page and Brodido in a Texas Deathmatch at Full Gear on Saturday to win the AEW World Trios Championships.

The rivalry pitting Swerve and The New Level against Page and Brodido over the trios titles began back in August at All In when Kofi and Austin Creed made their AEW debuts.

Kofi and Creed were revealed as Strickland's mystery partners in the Trios Roulette Royale, and they went on to win it to become the new AEW world trios champs.

Page, Brody King and Bandido were granted a rematch at All Out the following month, but Swerve and The New Level were successful in their first pay-per-view defense.

The feud didn't end there, though, as Hangman and Brodido were given one more title opportunity at WrestleDream, this time with a two-out-of-three falls stipulation.

Page and Brodido managed to win back the trios titles, making for a tense and awkward situation after the match.

While Kofi and Creed were more than willing to give Page and Brodido their flowers and recognize them as the new champions, a clearly agitated Strickland refused to shake hands with their opponents.

Coming out of WrestleDream, Swerve went to great lengths to attempt to goad Page and Brodido into a Texas Deathmatch.

While the Texas Deathmatch is Hangman's specialty, he was clearly hesitant to go back down that road after losing a Texas Deathmatch to Strickland at Full Gear 2023 and losing another to MJF at Revolution 2026.

However, amid Swerve's constant attempts to embarrass and disrespect him, Bandido essentially begged Page to accept the stipulation, and he ultimately did.

Page's uncertainty may have come back to haunt him and Bandido, as Strickland and The New Level prevailed and won back the trios titles.

articles.title: Ilja Dragunov vs. Tommaso Ciampa AEW National Title Match Winner, Top Highlights from Full Gear 2026
articles.summary: Ilja Dragunov beat Tommaso Ciampa at Full Gear on Saturday to win the National Championship, giving him his first title since joining AEW.
articles.body:
Ilja Dragunov beat Tommaso Ciampa at Full Gear on Saturday to win the National Championship, giving him his first title since joining AEW.

The clash between Ciampa and Dragunov came together quickly after Ciampa defeated Andrade El Idolo to become the new national champion on the Nov. 7 episode of Collision.

Ciampa had a successful title defense against "Speedball" Mike Bailey days later on Dynamite, and following his victory, Ciampa was interrupted by Dragunov.

A furious Ciampa pulled Dragunov off the ropes during his entrance, leading to an argument and Dragunov pointed at the big screen to show that Ciampa vs. Dragunov was official for Full Gear.

Dragunov then went for a handshake, only for Ciampa to flip him off, making it clear that there would be no mutual respect.

Both Ciampa and Dragunov are fairly recent additions to the AEW roster, and it hasn't taken them long to make an impact.

Ciampa joined AEW in January 2026 and won gold in his first match, beating Mark Briscoe for the TNT Championship. Although his reign lasted less than two weeks, Ciampa went on to win a number of matches against big names, including Chris Jericho.

Dragunov came to AEW last month, making his debut at WrestleDream, and beating Bailey in his debut match.

Ciampa and Dragunov have plenty of history, facing each other in singles matches in Germany's wXw promotion in 2015 and in WWE just last year.

That familiarity yielded a great match at Full Gear, and while Dragunov secured the first victory to become national champion, there may be many more encounters to come.

articles.title: Mercedes Mone vs. Marina Shafir AEW Women's Title Match Winner, Top Highlights from Full Gear 2026
articles.summary: Mercedes Moné defeated Marina Shafir at Full Gear on Saturday to retain the AEW Women's World Championship.
articles.body:
Mercedes Moné defeated Marina Shafir at Full Gear on Saturday to retain the AEW Women's World Championship.

Moné and Shafir began their rivalry on the heels of last month's WrestleDream pay-per-view, which saw Mercedes successfully defend the women's world title in a physical encounter with Thekla.

Following her victory, Mercedes took the opportunity to hold a celebration on Dynamite as she so often does, but Shafir crashed the party.

The Death Riders member questioned The CEO's toughness and vowed to take the AEW Women's World Championship from her.

Mercedes vs. Marina was made official for Full Gear shortly thereafter, but there were plenty of mind games left to be played between them.

Moné suggested that Shafir was only relevant because of Jon Moxley and The Death Riders, which was an implication that seemed to get under Marina's skin.

Shafir countered by saying that she was often the one behind many of the misdeeds The Death Riders committed in the past, underscoring her ruthless demeanor.

Given her status as a former MMA fighter, the hard-hitting Shafir aimed to break Moné both physically and mentally at Full Gear.

While Shafir may have had the strength and grappling advantage over Mercedes, she gave up a huge experience edge to The CEO in big-time, championship bouts.

That experience seemed to tip the scales in Moné's favor, as she bested Shafir to continue her nearly three-month reign as AEW women's world champ.

articles.title: Kayla Harrison Beats Amanda Nunes, Judges' Scorecards, Prize Money, Stats & Highlights from UFC 334
articles.summary: Kayla Harrison cemented a signature win and held on to the women's bantamweight title with a fourth-round submission win over Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 from Madison Square Garden in New York City.
articles.body:
Kayla Harrison cemented a signature win and held on to the women's bantamweight title with a fourth-round submission win over Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 from Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Harrison locked in a rear-naked choke on an exhausted Nunes after an impressive performance from the champion.

Both women were coming of long layoffs, but it didn't take them long to get back in the action.

Harrison pressed the issue as the aggressor with her footwork. Nunes responded with timely counters that rocked her early.

Then The Lioness made a mistake that cost her the second half of the round. She tried to take Harrison's back and ended up getting taken down and put in a crucifix. Harrison dominated the position the rest of the round and landed serious ground strikes.

Nunes continued her questionable strategy of engaging Harrison in grappling in the second frame. Harrison once again got to the crucifix position and did damage. Plenty were baffled by Nunes' strategy.

Meanwhile, Harrison continued to find herself in the better position:

The levy finally broke in the fourth round when Harrison knocked Nunes down and jumped on the rear-naked choke to draw the finish.

According to ESPN's Fight Center , Harrison landed 160 total strikes before getting the submission.

Harrison has long been considered one of the top fighters in all of women's MMA. Now she has a win against an all-time great to prove it.

The 36-year-old's rise to prominence in the sport started with her Olympic Judo career where she was a two-time gold medalist. That obviously drew comparisons to Ronda Rousey.

As it turns out, Harrison has proven herself to have more longevity in MMA than the Rowdy one. Harrison started competing in PFL in 2018 and has risen to the ranks of champion in the UFC.

The biggest problem for her has been the cut to 135. She spent much of her PFL career at 155 and 145 pounds before having to cut down to bantamweight to compete in the UFC.

Now, Harrison is calling for the organization to bring back her home weight class for a rematch with Nunes.

"I feel like I am gonna prove I'm the champion on on Saturday night," Harrison said at the UFC 334 pre-fight press conference . "And then I'll give her an automatic rematch at 145 so I can snatch that other belt."

The UFC briefly made the 145-pound class a division when Cyborg and Nunes were competing regularly. However, it has been defunct since 2023.

Nunes was making her first appearance since successfully defending her bantamweight title against Irene Aldana in 2023.

We'll have to see if her return from retirement was a one-off venture because of Harrison or if she has the competitive fire to keep pursuing the belt after the loss.

articles.title: Death Riders vs. The Cut Anarchy in the Arena Winner, Top Highlights from AEW Full Gear 2026
articles.summary: The Cut defeated The Death Riders and The Conglomeration in an Anarchy in the Arena match at AEW Full Gear on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Cut defeated The Death Riders and The Conglomeration in an Anarchy in the Arena match at AEW Full Gear on Saturday.

The victory came after Phoenix Suns mascot Go the Gorilla joined in on the action on the side of The Death Riders.

A new super-stable recently came together and threatened The Death Riders' positioning within AEW when The Dogs and The Bang Bang Gang agreed to join forces to form The Cut.

As part of the union, The Dogs kicked Gabe Kidd out of their group and The Cut attacked him, which put them firmly in The Death Riders' crosshairs since Kidd was a dual member of both The Death Riders and The Dogs.

Jon Moxley and Daniel Garcia attempted to get revenge on behalf of Kidd when they faced Jay White and David Finlay on the Oct. 28 episode of Dynamite, but White and Finlay were victorious thanks to interference from the other members of The Cut.

Following the loss, Mox challenged The Cut to an Anarchy in the Arena match at Full Gear, and given their numbers advantage, The Cut quickly accepted.

The Death Riders have made their fair share of enemies over the years, so it was fair to wonder if they would be able to find additional members for their team.

Despite having many battles with The Conglomeration, that faction agreed to unify with The Death Riders at Full Gear in the name of taking down a common enemy.

With that, Anarchy in the Arena was officially set with Moxley, Kidd, Garcia, Wheeler Yuta, Orange Cassidy, Roderick Strong and Kyle O'Reilly meeting White, Finlay, Juice Robinson, Clark Connors, Ace Austin, Colten Gunn and Austin Gunn.

The Death Riders entered the match with a ton of Anarchy in the Arena experience, which could have given them an advantage, but the uncertainty regarding how they would co-exist with The Conglomeration loomed large.

At Full Gear, The Cut proved the strength of their bond by taking down The Death Riders and The Conglomeration in their first major victory as a unit.

articles.title: Ciryl Gane Beats Josh Hokit, Judges' Scorecards, Prize Money, Stats & Highlights from UFC 334
articles.summary: Ciryl Gane successfully derailed the Josh Hokit hype train with a unanimous decision victory to defend his heavyweight title in the UFC 334 main event from Madison Square Garden.
articles.body:
Ciryl Gane successfully derailed the Josh Hokit hype train with a unanimous decision victory to defend his heavyweight title in the UFC 334 main event from Madison Square Garden.

Unsurprisingly, Hokit wasted no time in trying to impose his will on the fight. He charged at Gane from the opening bell and shot for an immediate takedown. He was able to get Gane to the mat, but it didn't last long.

Some of Hokit's momentum was halted by an eye poke from Gane. That was sure to be a controversial moment given Gane's history with accidental eye pokes.

However, Hokit recovered well enough to pick up Gane and drop him late in the first frame.

Hokit's aggression didn't really slow down in the second round. He stayed right in front of the champion and pushed the pace for the whole round.

Gane was landing. According to ESPN Fight Center , he actually landed more strikes than Hokit, but the challenger's pressure was clearly impacting his gameplan. Hokit was dragging Gane into deep waters to test his mettle in the championship rounds.

Gane found more success in those championship rounds. He started going to shorter strikes in the clinch and increased his body work to slow Hokit down.

The 36-year-old continued to finish out the fight strong, opening up his striking game and finishing the fight with 252 significant strikes landed, per ESPN Fight Center.

The win further cements Gane as the champion of the division, even if Tom Aspinall still looms.

This was technically Gane's first fight as the official champion of the division. He initially won the interim championship when he defeated Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250.

However, that's because of some unfinished business between Gane and Tom Aspinall. The 33-year-old's fight with Gane ended in a No Contest after an accidental eye poke ended the fight.

Unfortunately, Aspinall still hasn't returned. He has had multiple surgeries to address the eye injury he suffered in their bout. Gane became the undisputed heavyweight champion in Aspinall's absence.

"Yes of course," Gane said when asked if he has to beat Aspinall to feel like the undisputed champion. "I hope a speedy recovery for him, and then we're going to have a rematch for sure. Everyone wants to see this fight."

Gane feels as though he was winning the fight when the accidental eye poke happened in the first round, but there's still a feeling of the division being unresolved.

Aspinall has not set a timetable for when he'll be able to return to action so it's possible that Gane will have to fight someone else in his next defense.

For now, Gane sits atop the division as the undisputed king with a notable challenger vanquished.

articles.title: Gane, Hokit, Amanda Nunes, Kayla Harrison's Next Best Fights After UFC 334 Results
articles.summary: UFC 334 saw two belts up for grabs as Ciryl Gane and Kayla Harrison came away as the heavyweight champion and women's bantamweight titleholder.
articles.body:
UFC 334 saw two belts up for grabs as Ciryl Gane and Kayla Harrison came away as the heavyweight champion and women's bantamweight titleholder.

Gane now presides over a division that is always full of surprises. Tom Aspinall still looms as the top contender, but Alexander Volkov and Alex Pereira are still in the title picture.

Harrison not only controls their division but stands out as the biggest star on their side of the sport right now. She will now have a target on her back in a division with a few fighters looking to break out.

Let's break down the next best opponents for all four of the featured fighters from UFC 334.

Sergei Pavlovich vs. Alex Pereira winner

Ciryl Gane once again got his hand raised and retained his heavyweight title. He has established himself as the top heavyweight in the UFC, but there are always some heavy hitters ready to take that title away.

In an ideal world, we'd finally be able to see if Tom Aspinall can settle some unfinished business with the champion. Aspinall has been out of commission since their UFC 321 bout ended in a No Contest due to an accidental eye poke by Gane.

Aspinall has not returned since then and has undergone multiple surgeries to address the eye injury that stopped the fight, but has yet to announce an official return date.

If Aspinall still isn't ready to return then Alexander Volkov probably has the cleanest case to be he next contender. Volkov has a split-decision loss to Gane on his record and has rattled off three wins in a row since that loss.

Gane beat Alex Pereira in Poatan's heavyweight debut, but it wouldn't be surprising if his December fight against Sergei Pavlovich played a role in the title picture. If the former light heavyweight star can beat Pavlovich it could set up the rematch.

At the same time, a win for Pavolovich would have four wins in a row including one over the biggest name in the division right now. That could be enough to tip the scales in his favor.

Josh Hokit's hype train led to a title shot, but the loss throws that train onto a little detour. Just how long Hokit stays out of the title picture depends on how he bounces back.

The reality is that the heavyweight division is fairly shallow right now. Hokit is a marketable fighter with enough skill to back up his brash personality.

Considering that drawing power and personality, the UFC might opt to continue to give him the biggest names possible. Volkov stands out as a title contender so giving Hokit a shot to take him out would keep him high in the rankings.

At the same time, they could look to that December 12 fight against Sergei Pavlovich and Alex Pereira to find his next opponent. The loser will also be looking to bounce back after losing a high stakes fight so the winner would come out with some momentum.

Going in the opposite direction, they could make Hokit the A-side to fight that pits him against a fellow rising contender. Vitor Perino has drawn attention with a four-fight win streak in the UFC.

Hokit would be a step up in competition for him nd a chance for Hokit to shine again.

Kayla Harrison finally got her chance to prove herself against a true star in the sport. After chasing the likes of Ronda Rousey and Nunes for stardom, she came through against the Lioness.

The next best move might be to run it back at 145 pounds.

The reality is that Harrison is more suited to fight at 145 pounds. The UFC shut down the women's featherweight division, but Harrison has already expressed interest in reviving it to set up a second fight with Nunes.

Moving up would not only give Harrison the distinction of being a two-weight champion, but it would also give her a second marquee fight against a big name.

The other options are to give the next generation of title contenders a shot at 135 pounds. Joselyne Edwards is the No. 1-ranked contender in the division and she's currently riding a four-fight win streak.

Ailin Perez also has an interesting case. She's won seven in a row, including a win against Edwards back in June 2024.

Taking on either of the younger contenders probably comes down to whether Harrison is willing to continue to cut all the way down to 135 pounds.

The Lioness came up short in her bid to win the title in her comeback fight. Nunes had been retired since June 2023, but wanted to come back to be champion again.

In truth, she doesn't need to keep fighting for her legacy. She's already a UFC hall of famer. She was one of the most dominant champions in the sport and has the best resume of any fighter in the sport.

No one would blame Nunes for walking away. But if she is still interested in tying up some loose ends and potentially fighting for the belt again then there are good options.

Julianna Pena might be the best available. There's some narrative juice there with their prior history. Pena stunned Nunes at UFC 269 with a submission before Nunes got her revenge at UFC 289.

Now the series sits at one apiece and the two could close the book with a rubber match before either of them retires.

If Nunes is more eager to take on the best in the division then Ailin Perez is the clear answer. She is on a seven-fight win streak that actually includes a win over Joselyn Edwards.

articles.title: Zelfa Barrett stops Gavin Gwynne for vacant WBA Intercontinental lightweight title
articles.summary: Zelfa Barrett claimed the vacant WBA Intercontinental lightweight title with a fifth-round stoppage of Gavin Gwynne at Wembley Arena.
articles.body:
Zelfa Barrett claimed the vacant WBA Intercontinental lightweight title with a fifth-round stoppage of Gavin Gwynne at Wembley Arena.

Former British, Commonwealth and European lightweight champion Gwynne was five inches taller than his opponent but was floored by an uppercut from the quicker fighter.

Manchester's Barrett, 33, extended his record to 36 wins and three defeats with 19 knockouts, and has won five fights in a row.

Gwynne went into the fight on the back of an impressive majority decision win over previously unbeaten Khaleel Majid in May.

However, the 36-year-old, from Merthyr in south Wales, now has a record of 19-5-2.

Barrett will hope victory on the MF Pro card gives him a chance to move up the WBA rankings at 135lbs.

articles.title: Swerve Strickland, Kyle Fletcher, Real Winners and Losers of AEW Full Gear Match Card
articles.summary: All Elite Wrestling returned to the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona for Full Gear 2026.
articles.body:
All Elite Wrestling returned to the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona for Full Gear 2026.

It was a special night that included the latest chapters in the rivalries of Hangman Adam Page vs. Swerve Strickland and Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher.

In the biggest match of her career, Marina Shafir challenged Mercedes Moné while The Death Riders and Conglomeration aligned to battle The Cut in Anarchy in the Arena.

Who would won big on this night? Who fell short as the end of 2026 rapidly approaches?

Queen Aminata officially signed with AEW for the first time in 2024. Full Gear was the first time she walked into a pay-per-view as champion.

It was also the first time she walked out as champion.

While it was a last-minute adjustment to a 4-Way battle for the gold, The Queen remains strong as TBS champion.

Hopefully, she will make more than just the Tailgate Brawl next time around, but Aminata should have plenty of chances in what should be a lengthy run.

The former champion Persephone remains the most obvious threat to Aminata, but it is hard to imagine the title will bounce right back to the former champion.

Instead, it will take time to create a fresh threat to The Queen that has not held the title before.

Adam Copeland knows that his time is rapidly approaching to end a legendary career, but Kazuchika Okada may have just made The Rated-R Superstar question if he can even make it to 2027.

This was a physical battle to start the show that favored Okada early and often. No matter how many times Cope countered The Rainmaker, he was quickly shut down.

Despite the International Championship on the line, it never truly looked like a fair PPV bout.

Cope will want revenge on Okada at some point after this contest, but it is hard to imagine that he could ever beat The Rainmaker after this.

This is certainly not the end yet for The Rated-R Superstar, but it is the biggest loss he has suffered since arriving in AEW.

While it was not Mark Davis and Joke Doyle's night, they delivered by far the best match of their career as a team.

This was a spectacular performance from the big men against The Young Bucks, once again showing the way that Matt and Nick Jackson elevate their opponents.

By the end of this, it was clear that as good as other teams in The Don Callis Family have been, this is the best team that The Family has.

Both men can be dominant forces in singles and tag action going forward, and it would be a shock and disappointment if they do not win gold together in 2027.

Winner: The Kasper Brothers (Formerly The Creed Brothers)

When word came out that Julius and Brutus Creed had mutually agreed to not re-sign in WWE, it was hard to completely call where they would land next.

It probably should have been an easy call though to expect they would join an AEW that has planted the flag as the tag team wrestling company in the world.

Even so, no one could have called The Kasper Brothers going from losing in NXT to debuting in direct conflict with the AEW world tag team champions.

This was a rousing endorsement for The Kasper Brothers, who were immediately compared to The Steiner Brothers while working with FTR.

As AEW establishes itself all the more as the place for tag team wrestling, The Kasper Brothers look poised to quickly challenge for the top prize, hoping to prove themselves next to The Young Bucks and Motor City Machine Guns.

Clearly based on Brutus' first comments directly to the camera at Full Gear, they have high hopes for their future.

The World Trios Championships were on the line in an absolutely brutal Texas Death Match that lived up to its role as a sequel to the Hangman Adam Page vs. Swerve Strickland Texas Death Match.

By the end, it was clear that New Level belonged in AEW, taking scary and gory spots to sell the intensity of this rivalry.

However, even more so, The Mogul completed his most heinous plan to date, taking down The Cowboy in the center of the ring to win this contest.

He defeated all of his most dangerous recent enemies and dragged Kofi and Austin Creed down to his violent level to get back the World Trios Championships.

It was a rousing success and finally allows Swerve to fully embrace his role once more as AEW's Most Dangerous Man.

On paper, Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron were not supposed to be the team to take down the undefeated Brawling Birds.

However, as AEW continues to build up a fresh women's tag division, it is important to clearly establish the teams that will be fighting for those titles for years to come.

Wrathlander is now one of those teams after becoming the first team in AEW to pin The Brawling Birds, capturing the Women's World Tag Team Championships.

Based on the pre-entrance video package, Tony Khan is a big fan of Wrathlander, and this could be a more dominant team going forward than anyone could have expected.

Hopefully it will be a more substantial run for Harley than her first reign with Willow Nightingale that was cut short to push Willow into singles action.

Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor took down Divine Dominion not once but twice to definitively crown themselves the best women's tag team in AEW.

The Brawling Birds were supposed to dominate as Women's tag team champions into the new year.

Instead, after a shocking ending, Hayter and Windsor could find themselves on the outside looking into title pictures in AEW.

The next goal for The Brawling Birds will be prove they did not only win the gold at All In because it was in their home country.

Hayter and Windsor should remain central players in this tag division, but it would not be immediately effective for them to regain the gold. They need to work their way back.

It was good to see Ilja Dragunov win big in his first PPV match in AEW, an expected big statement by the company to back Unbesiegbar immediately.

However, it is a shame that it came at the expense of The Psycho Killer, who has played transitional champion twice in his first year in AEW.

This could be an intentional character journey for Ciampa, but it does look disrespectful for now of a man that has consistently over-delivered in his AEW transition.

Ciampa not only deserves a lengthy title reign but also has shown fans why they should want to see The Psycho Killer as a long-term champion.

Marina Shafir has never looked better than on this night.

Helped both by working with Mercedes Moné and fueled by the need to prove herself as a true Death Rider, The Problem looked unstoppable at times.

The win in the ring did not come, but Shafir absolutely showed she could hang with the best in AEW, selling herself as a future champion.

Everyone in attendance believed in Shafir down the stretch, and The CEO had to steal the pin to survive.

It would not be surprising to see AEW book a rematch between these two, and it would even not be surprising if Shafir beats Moné in that rematch.

At the end of an utterly absurd Anarchy in the Arena that included Go the Gorilla, DMX and KeMalito, The Cut somehow stoked the momentum of The Death Riders and won.

In particular, "Switchblade" Jay White pinned the Continental champion and his biggest rival in AEW, Jon Moxley.

The Cut was formed to combat The Death Riders, and despite the full crew appearing for this fight, they accomplished their mission in the first fight.

Switchblade has built momentum into the Continental Classic. The Dogs, The Gunns and Ace Austin all gained serious credibility as well.

No matter what comes next, The Cut already looks like a real threat for the long haul thanks to this victory in Anarchy in the Arena.

Kyle Fletcher promised this was the match that would prove he is better than Will Ospreay, yet at the end of the night, The Aerial Assassin stood tall.

This was a personal loss for The Protostar that he cannot easily recover from.

There is no one Fletcher has defined himself more by than Ospreay, yet once again, The Aerial Assassin beat him.

Ospreay did not come into this match with a question for himself. It was a question to Fletcher if he was ready to step up to the next level.

Arguably, The Protostar did just that, competing at a main event level with the top man in AEW right now, but that was not what Fletcher needed.

He needed to beat Ospreay, and this was not his night.

articles.title: MJF Returns After Will Ospreay Beats Kyle Fletcher, Top Highlights from AEW Title Match at Full Gear
articles.summary: Will Ospreay defeated Kyle Fletcher at Full Gear on Saturday to retain the AEW World Championship.
articles.body:
Will Ospreay defeated Kyle Fletcher at Full Gear on Saturday to retain the AEW World Championship.

After the win, MJF returned to AEW programming for the first time since All In at the end of August and attacked Ospreay.

Ospreay and Fletcher have a ton of history with each other, but Full Gear marked the first time they ever faced off in a singles bout for a North American world title.

Before officially joining AEW, Ospreay and Fletcher were stablemates in United Empire, and they were also both part of The Don Callis Family in 2023 and 2024 until Ospreay left the group.

That moment led to the elevation of both Ospreay and Fletcher, as Ospreay eventually went on to become world champ, while Fletcher became a world title contender and holder of both the TNT and International Championships.

Fletcher recently positioned himself as the No. 1 contender for the AEW world title by teaming with Kevin Knight to beat Ospreay and Adam Copeland in a tag team match on the Oct. 21 episode of Dynamite.

After the big victory, Fletcher referred to himself as the uncrowned AEW world champion and challenged Ospreay to a world title match at Full Gear, which led to Ospreay accepting.

Saturday marked the fifth one-on-one meeting between Ospreay and Fletcher since they came to AEW.

While Ospreay led the series 3-1, Fletcher's victory occurred at Full Gear 2024, which potentially could have given him a psychological edge at the same pay-per-view two years later.

On top of that, Fletcher's tag team win over Ospreay had him looking like a legitimate threat to dethrone his former ally.

Even so, Ospreay prevailed in yet another difficult test, adding Fletcher to the list of those he has beaten since becoming AEW world champion along with Jon Moxley, Kazuchika Okada and others.

articles.title: The Real Winners and Losers From UFC 334
articles.summary: It was fight night. It was Madison Square Garden.
articles.body:
It was fight night. It was Madison Square Garden.

Which made it a particularly big fight night in midtown Manhattan, where Dana White and Co. touched down with a UFC 334 show that was topped by two title fights.

The B/R combat team was in the house from the earliest prelim to the final strike of the main event and compiled a list of the event's definitive winners and losers.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

Ciryl Gane became the UFC's heavyweight champion under dubious circumstances after his fight with Tom Aspinall ended thanks to an eye poke that prompted Aspinall, who'd arrived as the incumbent, to later announce he'd vacated the belt due to injury.

So, when Gane arrived to defend against streaking contender Josh Hokit, who'd worked himself into the opportunity with a series of impressive wins and bombastic interviews, it wasn't hard to find people who doubted the champ's ability to handle the challenge.

The fact that he'd lost to Jon Jones in 124 seconds didn't help the perception.

Though the chatty Hokit was frenetic and intermittently effective through the first three rounds, his gas tank dipped toward E across the final 10 minutes and allowed Gane to retake the initiative on the way to 48-47 tallies on all three official scorecards.

"This guy is a mother**ker," Gane said. "He did very well."

Amanda Nunes is a slam-dunk Hall of Famer. Perhaps the greatest female ever.

But the official record shows her magical UFC run ended with a 16-2 record more than three years ago, where she handled Irene Aldana by a wide unanimous decision.

And by the time she climbed into the cage to meet Kayla Harrison for the bantamweight title that the Ohioan had captured in Nunes's absence, it was clear her time had passed.

The Brazilian's interrupted run as the top woman in the sport officially ended in the fourth round when Harrison caught her attempt to land a right-legged kick, spun her to the floor and immediately pounced with a strike before locking in the rear-naked choke that prompted "The Lioness" to tap in surrender at 1:29.

It was her first loss since Julianna Pena beat her, also by rear-naked choke, in 2021.

Walkaway fights don't go as well as it did for Stephen Thompson.

But the popular welterweight striking savant not only left the UFC on his own terms, but he did it in signature style—flattening Charles Radtke with a right-legged spinning heel kick that led to the fight's abrupt end at 2:54 of Round 3.

The win let Thompson finish his UFC run at 13-9-1 with seven KOs and ended a nearly four-year drought since his most recent win against Kevin Holland in December 2022.

He'd fought more fights than anyone in UFC history. And he'd won more fights than anyone in UFC history. But neither record did Jim Miller any good on Saturday night.

Instead, he ran into an aggressive and hungry 32-year-old in Terrance McKinney and was squashed by a left hand to the chin just past the midway point of Round 1 in a bout that was fought at 160 pounds after McKinney missed the 155-pound limit on Friday.

It was the first time Miller lost inside the distance since Charles Oliveira choked him out in 2018. McKinney, for the record, said he'd move to welterweight (170) for his next fight.

Middleweight Donte Johnson arrived with a pristine record (9-0), an interesting nickname ("Lockjaw") and status as a significant betting favorite heading into his prelim scrap with 38-year-old veteran Cesar Almeida.

Johnson, who'd won three in the UFC and once on the Contender Series, came out fast and looked for an eighth first-round finish, but Almeida survived the storm and ultimately dumped Johnson to the floor with a right hand midway through the first.

He eventually rose, but a follow-up barrage along the fence prompted a stoppage at 3:20.

It's hard to find people not excited by Bia Mesquita.

The 35-year-old Brazilian arrived to the UFC with a 5-0 record and reeled off her fourth straight octagonal win on Saturday's early prelim card with a first-round submission via rear naked choke over No. 14 bantamweight contender Macy Chiasson.

Mesquita quickly got the fight to her comfort zone on the mat and pelted Chiasson with strikes on the way to locking in the choke that ended matters at 3:23.

articles.title: Harrison destroza a Nunes y Gane supera a Hokit en un UFC 334 histórico
articles.standfirst: La cartelera celebrada en el Madison Square Garden de Nueva York ha dejado momentos memorables y varias sorpresas
articles.summary: La cartelera celebrada en el Madison Square Garden de Nueva York ha dejado momentos memorables y varias sorpresas
articles.body: El UFC 334 celebrado en el Madison Square Garden de Nueva York ha dejado momentos históricos. En el combate co estelar, Kayla Harrison (20-1) ha dado una exhibición ante Amanda Nunes (23-6) para retener su título de peso gallo, y en la pelea estelar Ciryl Gane (15-2) superó a Josh Hokit (10-0) por decisión unánime para defender por primera vez el cinturón indiscutido de peso pesado y arruinar el sueño del estadounidense en uno de los combates del año. La pelea fue tal y como acostumbran las de Hokit: caos puro. El estadounidense avisó que iba a poner un ritmo inaguantable para Gane antes del duelo, y no mentía, ya que por mucho que se comiese demasiados jabs iba siempre hacia el frente. Por momentos Gane acusó la frustración de no poder finalizar a Josh, pero llegaron empatados a dos asaltos al quinto round y fue ahí donde 'Bon Gamin' tiró de experiencia para llevarse la decisión unanime. Aun así, honor para Hokit, ya que fue el principal culpable de que esta pelea sea una de las mejores del año y ha demostrado que tiene lo necesario para plantar cara a los mejores del mundo. Gane defiende por primera vez el cinturón y ahora esperará al ganador del Alex Pereira vs Sergei Pavlovich para conocer su siguiente rival, con permiso de Tom Aspinall. En el combate co estelar, Kayla Harrison hizo la mejor actuación de su carrera para someter a Amanda Nunes con un mataleón en el cuarto asalto que posiblemente la consagre como la mejor peleadora de todos los tiempos. Amanda volvía tras más de tres años sin pelear, y la estadounidense le dio un golpe de realidad gracias a su judo -doble medallista de oro olímpica- y a sus habilidades en el suelo. Hasta ahora, todo el mundo consideraba a Nunes la GOAT, pero la manera en la que ha ganado Harrison da pie a cierto debate incómodo sobre sí es ella la que debe ocupar ese puesto. La forma en la que ha ganado a 'The Lioness' no se había visto antes, y ahora está por ver si la brasileña decide seguir compitiendo o vuelve al retiro. Una de las mayores sorpresas del año la dio Luis Gurule (12-4), último verdugo de Dani Bárez en la UFC, que dio una lección en el grappling a Bilal Hasan (10-1, 1NC) y bajó todo el hype que había sobre la nueva 'superestrella' de peso mosca venciendo le por decisión unánime. Además, Caio Borralho (19-2, 1NC) tiró de experiencia para tumbar a Yousri Belgaroui (11-4) por decisión unánime, y Kevin Holland (29-15-1, 1NC) y Uros Medic (14-3-1) protagonizaron el momento más polémico de toda la cartelera poco tiempo después, ya que los jueces decidieron dar un empate mayoritario a pesar de que al peleador serbio le habían quitado un punto. Una decisión que traerá cola. De la cartelera preliminar también hay que destacar varias actuaciones, pero sin duda la mejor fue la de Stephen Thompson (18-9-1) en su pelea de retirada. 'Wonderboy' se despidió con un brutal K.O. a Charles Radtke (12-6) de patada giratoria que ya es historia. Menuda forma de decir adiós, con una de las mejores finalizaciones de su carrera en el Madison Square Garden. Otro nombre propio fue Terrance McKinney (19-9), que mantuvo su 100% de finalizaciones con un gran K.O. ante una leyenda como Jim Miller (39-20-1). Eso sí, esa pelea se dio porque Miller quiso, ya que McKinney había fallado el peso por mas de dos kilos. La gran sorpresa la dio César Almeida (8-3) noqueando a Donte Johnson (9-1) para quitarle el invicto, y Bea Mesquita (9-0) sí pudo mantener el suyo con una impresionante sumisión ante Myce Chiasson (11-7) en el primer asalto

articles.summary: Ciryl Gane dug himself out of an early hole and impressively found his second wind to outlast Josh Hokit and defend his UFC heavyweight title Saturday in the main event of UFC 334.
articles.body: For a moment, it appeared as if Josh Hokit was about to complete one of the most improbable rises to a title the UFC had ever seen. In the end, though, Ciryl Gane showed why he's long been considered one of the sport's elite heavyweights.Gane dug himself out of an early hole and impressively found his second wind to outlast Hokit and defend his UFC heavyweight title Saturday in the main event of UFC 334. After the previously undefeated challenger built an early lead with a tidal wave of forward pressure, Gane took over late and gutted out the championship rounds to claim a unanimous decision (48-47, 48-47, 48-47) inside New York's Madison Square Garden."This guy is a motherf***er. He did very well," an exhausted Gane said post-fight."He didn't surprise me. I knew already. All the people around the world underestimated him. Not me. This guy is the future. He did so well tonight. It was a tough fight."For Gane (15-2, 1 NC), that was the understatement of all understatements.Hokit (10-1) stormed out from the opening horn like a house afire, throwing a barrage of takedown attempts and punches in bunches, while never giving the Frenchman a single inch to breathe. It was a pace unlike few ever seen in a five-round heavyweight fight, and though Gane landed punches with frequency and consistency, it was clear that Hokit's awkwardness and relentlessness was having a draining effect on the champion.Making matters more impressive, Hokit shrugged off an early eye-poke from Gane, whose proclivity for fight-changing fouls has garnered quite a reputation in recent years.Josh Hokit was able to shrug off this first round eye poke by Ciryl Game 👁️🫵 #UFC334 pic.twitter.com/18cPmO2kqZ— Uncrowned (@uncrownedcombat) November 15, 2026 HUGE SLAM BY JOSH HOKIT 😳[ #UFC334 | LIVE on @paramountplus ] pic.twitter.com/Oqxs8H4jtY— UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) November 15, 2026 By the third round, Gane appeared to be fading heavily, as his corner implored him to rest on Hokit and conserve whatever energy he had left. Yet Hokit continued to apply nonstop pressure, battering Gane to the tune of a 71-37 advantage in total strikes throughout the frame while seemingly taking hold of every ounce of momentum.Hokit's decorated coaches, Greg Jackson and Mike Winkeljohn, told the former NFL player between the third and the fourth that he was 10 minutes away from becoming UFC heavyweight champion, and indeed, the outcome appeared to be a mere formality.Ciryl Gane's corner:"You gotta go on top and rest for two minutes. Rest on top of him."[ #UFC334 | LIVE on @paramountplus ] pic.twitter.com/iU6P852JYy— UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) November 15, 2026 But Gane, a man criticized in the past for allegedly lacking heart, summoned whatever strength he had left to retake control in the championship rounds. He fended off all 11 of Hokit's takedown attempts and out-struck his suddenly exhausted foe by a whopping margin of 158-84 in total strikes over the final 10 minutes to seal a come-from-behind win.In total, Gane's 237 significant strikes landed over the five-round affair marked a new single-fight UFC heavyweight record, surpassing the benchmark previously held by Daniel Cormier. With Hokit's 146 significant strikes, the duo also generated a new combined record for the most significant strikes ever seen in a UFC heavyweight fight.WE GO THE DISTANCEHow did you score it?[ #UFC334 | LIVE on @paramountplus ] pic.twitter.com/1k0KsTs0tf— UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) November 15, 2026 "That was a tough fight," Gane said. "That was hard [pace to match] when we started the fight, but I kept going, I kept going, because I'm strong.""I'm a warrior, he is too," Gane added. "It was an incredible fight."For Hokit, it's surely a discouraging end to one of the more abrupt rises we've seen in recent UFC history. The former fullback had rattled off four straight victories since making his promotional debut in late 2025, including big wins over Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis. A 29-year-old American who's courted controversy at every turn, Hokit would've completed one of the fastest runs ever to claiming an undisputed belt."I will rejoice in my suffering," he said post-fight. "Suffering builds endurance. Endurance builds character, and character builds hope. I will never lose hope. I will be champion one day. articles.title: UFC 334: Kayla Harrison shocks Amanda Nunes on UFC return to retain title
articles.summary: Kayla Harrison shocks returning great Amanda Nunes by submitting the former double champion to retain her bantamweight title at UFC 334 in New York.
articles.body:
Kayla Harrison shocked returning great Amanda Nunes by submitting the former double champion to retain her bantamweight title at UFC 334 in New York.

Nunes, 38, was fighting for the first time since she brought her glittering career to a close in 2023, after dominating at bantamweight and featherweight for years.

Enticed by the challenge of fighting Harrison, the Brazilian came out of retirement for the bout but could not topple her friend and former training partner.

Just 10 months after neck and spinal surgery, 36-year-old American Harrison ended the contest in the fourth round at Madison Square Garden with a rear-naked choke.

Afterwards, Harrison reflected on the challenges she's overcome during her career.

As a youngster, Harrison was sexually abused by her judo coach, who was sentenced to 10 years in prison after being found guilty.

Harrison went on to become a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo before moving into mixed martial arts where she became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion and then won UFC bantamweight gold in just her third fight in the organisation.

"I was sexually abused at a young age, statistically I'm not supposed to be here," said Harrison.

"If you'd told me at six years old this would be my life and at 16, I wouldn't have believed you.

"I'm really grateful, humbled and it's an honour and privilege to stand before you."

In the main event, heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Josh Hokit.

In a gruelling contest which featured a record 383 significant strikes in a UFC heavyweight bout, Frenchman Gane's counter striking off the back foot proved the difference.

Harrison cements status as all-time great

Nunes left the UFC in 2023 as the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts.

During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko, but it was the prospect of fighting Harrison which brought her out of retirement.

The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, which Nunes left in 2022.

Nunes started well and stung Harrison with a number of straight rights, but found herself in trouble at the end of the round with the American in a dominant position on the ground.

Despite appearing to have an advantage on the feet, Nunes continued to try and grapple but it was a tactic which played into Harrison's hands.

Harrison took the fight to the floor with a powerful hip toss, before later cutting Nunes with a big elbow and right hand on the ground.

The decisive moment came in the fourth round as Harrison caught a kick before throwing Nunes off-balance and locking in the fight-ending submission.

After the fight, Harrison said she was considering retirement after admitting difficulties in cutting down to 135lb (9st 9lb).

"I've got a lot of decisions to make when I get home. Every time I make weight I say never again," she said.

"I've definitely got some injuries after that fight, I'll need to heal up."

The win was Harrison's 20th in 21 fights, solidifying her status as one of the best combat sports athletes of all time.

Nunes, whose legacy is already cemented, suffered the sixth defeat of her 29-fight career.

Gane outlasts Hokit for first title defence

Gane was making the first defence of his heavyweight title since being upgraded to undisputed champion in September after Tom Aspinall vacated the belt.

American Hokit was fighting for the belt after only one year in the organisation, with some critics arguing that he didn't deserve the title fight.

The 28-year-old's performance against Gane, however, shows he belongs among the division's top competition.

Hokit applied relentless pressure from the start, swarming Gane with takedown attempts and punches, with the 36-year-old looking to land counter shots.

Like in his fight against Aspinall, Gane poked Hokit in the eyes, but he was able to shrug it off before unleashing a huge slam at the end of the round.

Hokit's relentless pace continued with a tiring Gane looking surprised at the American's intensity.

Despite the pressure from Hokit however, Gane was the fighter landing more consistently from the back foot.

Gane used his jab effectively and eventually Hokit tired in the later rounds, allowing the champion to take control and see out victory.

Victory sets up a rematch against Aspinall, should the Briton make a full recovery from an eye injury.

On the undercard, British lightweight Chris Duncan beat American Drew Dober by unanimous decision.

The Scotsman had a four-fight win streak ended by Renato Moicano in April, but he returned to winning ways to secure his seventh win in nine UFC fights.

Stephen Thompson brought his 16-year career to a close in style as he stopped fellow American Charles Radtke with a trademark spinning wheel kick.

Former welterweight title challenger Thompson retired after the contest, with the 43-year-old leaving the sport having won 18 of his 28 professional bouts.
