articles.title: AEW Full Gear: 8 big takeaways after Anarchy in the Arena and Texas Death steal the show
articles.summary: As we hit the home stretch of 2026, here's eight big takeaways from a wild night in Phoenix for AEW Full Gear.
articles.body:
Will Ospreay closed out AEW Full Gear 2026 from the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix with another successful world championship title defense. Across the rest of Saturday's card, Mercedes Moné held on to her title, Swerve Strickland and The New Level survived a Texas Death Match, Jay White pinned Jon Moxley, Wrathlander became tag-team champs, the Young Bucks retained their titles, Tommaso Ciampa stumbled yet again with an AEW title, and Kazuchika Okada pinned Adam Copeland.

As we hit the home stretch of 2026, here's eight big takeaways from a wild night in the desert.

The depth of story AEW has been able to build up and down its roster is genuinely remarkable. Kyle Fletcher's ability to pick up his history with Will Ospreay and implement it throughout Saturday's main-event match was simply exceptional; from the challenger showing how much he's grown since they last mixed it up — bouncing the champ off of him when Ospreay attempted a Hidden Blade — all the way to the finish, which saw a Tiger Driver being the difference-maker for Ospreay to retain.

Since Fletcher's previous attempt at claiming AEW's top prize in September, he's experienced enormous growth as the challenger. It was quite clear from the beginning that Ospreay is destined to be on a lengthy world title run, but Fletcher was almost perfect in a match that felt like his coming out moment. And even more importantly, it felt like he belonged every step of the way. There was emotion, physicality, and the story told inside Saturday's ring elevated both men.

This match was likely a one-off, as MJF attacked Ospreay from behind afterward, while Andrade El Idolo still lingers with his guaranteed title shot as well. But there's no question that Fletcher has officially jumped into the main-event picture as a world title contender.

At the same time, this isn't the same Ospreay that got close but couldn't close the deal in years past. He's ruthless, willing to pull the trigger for whatever it takes to ensure he holds onto his belt. That mentality has followed him in both emotionally and physically taxing matches against Kenny Omega, Jon Moxley, and now Fletcher.

Marina Shafir has been searching for her breakout moment since joining AEW. Saturday night offered quite the opportunity for her to take a step forward as a legitimate challenger for the world title against one of the greatest of all time, Mercedes Moné.

Moné did what she does best, making Shafir look the part throughout their back-and-forth match. The duo leaned on their technical prowess, with Shafir mixing in callbacks to her Death Rider partners throughout. The finish saw Moné turn the Statement Maker into a Brutalizer — an ode to PAC — before Shafir rolled over and locked in a Brutalizer of her own. The champ then rolled Shafir over and grabbed the ropes with her own feet to retain the belt.

The flukey nature of Saturday's finish opens the door for more, with Shafir and Moné already mixing it up again later in the evening. AEW is better with more contenders for the world title, and the promotion seems focused on ensuring it's building a roster of women where it wouldn't be a surprise to see any of them holding the belt.

Swerve Strickland promised brutality, and the former world champ delivered.

For nearly an hour, Strickland and "Hangman" Adam Page dragged Austin Creed, Kofi, Bandido and Brody King into their vortex of violence.

The New Level were thrust right into what their night would involve, having skewers jammed into their heads within minutes of Saturday's match starting. The Texas Death Match featured blood from the beginning, and a barrage of weapons — barbed wire trumpets, a full glass window, a cinderblock, thumbtacks embedded in a glove, and so much more.

Brodido and the New Level played their roles perfectly as supplemental characters to the main story between Strickland and Page. The quartet picked their spots, sliding in and out of focus with one another as they fought off the other challengers. To culminate the violent delights, Strickland knocked Page out with a House Call to keep "Hangman" on the mat as the referee counted to 10.

For the second time, Strickland has defeated Page in a Texas Death Match, now claiming the Trios Championship in the process. All six men in this match have carried out devastation in recent months, and while it's hard to imagine them continuing it from here, it's even more difficult to envision a world where they aren't escalating things further.

Perhaps the impending Continental Classic will offer some reprieve from what is AEW's hottest rivalry.

On a card that already had an absolutely brutal Texas Death Match, Anarchy in the Arena had plenty of ground to make up.

The Death Riders, The Conglomeration and The Cut did everything to differentiate their match from the violence of Texas Death, battling all throughout the arena to a soundtrack of DMX's "Party Up." The match kicked off even before the opening bell; it had surprise appearances by Shane Taylor Promotions, Mercedes Moné, Marina Shafir, Willow Nightingale and KeMalito; and had what felt like nonstop action.

This year's Anarchy in the Arena paired a heavy amount of blood with the depth of stories like Gabe Kidd turning down an opportunity to join The Cut mid-match. KeMalito took a wild dropkick to the outside, Kidd was slammed through a flaming table, Orange Cassidy was speared through the stage, and the finish saw Jay White pin Jon Moxley for the win.

The easy route here would've been a guy like Moxley or Cassidy earning the pinfall. But The Cut needed to establish itself, and the fact that it was Moxley who ate the loss, with White standing tall alongside his newly formed faction, speaks volumes about what AEW sees in the title contender.

White's been bitten by the injury bug off and on throughout his AEW tenure, but it'd appear Tony Khan is determined to get the most out of White at the top of the card. A signature win like this should go far in establishing him as someone who isn't far off from challenging for the world title.

Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron's run to the AEW Women's Tag Team Championship was an unlikely one, but the duo didn't let that stop them from a shocking victory over the Brawling Birds to claim the belts. Statlander and Cameron met Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor every step of the way, putting together a back-and-forth tilt that saw the challengers reverse Two Birds, One Stone, leading to the finish. Statlander landed Saturday Night Fever, while Cameron held off Hayter as the duo claimed the belts.

The return to championship gold is nothing but positive for Statlander, whose brief world title run ended with her picking up the pieces without a clear direction. Alongside Cameron, she suddenly seems revitalized and has an avenue to establish their team atop AEW's tag division.

Perhaps it's an unpopular opinion, but really the only thing I dislike about this current iteration of AEW is that there are a million factions. Factions embedded in factions, even. I have no qualms with the Brawling Birds being in matching gear, and I get Alex Windsor is married to the men's world champ, Will Ospreay. But I really don't need the AEW version of United Empire, and I just don't see the benefit of building so many factions. It's almost a mark against your character if you're not aligned with a faction at this point. We're looking at you, MJF.

Almost as soon as Tommaso Ciampa's hands clasped around the AEW National Championship, it was written in the stars that he wouldn't have a sustained run with the belt.

Just seven days later, Ilja Dragunov became Ciampa's successor in a hard-fought, back-and-forth tilt. The champ did everything but get his hand raised, as Ciampa and Dragunov traded targeting each other's limbs. Ultimately, Dragunov landed a D-Bomb to put Ciampa down for the three count.

It's no surprise to see Dragunov being thrust into the spotlight with championship gold. The possibilities are endless for how far he goes in AEW, as someone whose wrestling style is tailor made for the promotion.

For Ciampa, it'll be interesting to see how he wraps his 2026. One of the bright spots on the roster, Ciampa has been an unquestioned star throughout his limited run in AEW and seems to make the most with his television time. But his inability to build momentum is concerning this early into his tenure. For each step forward, it feels like Ciampa is taking an equal step backward. And with that, it's hard to trust Ciampa as a legit contender.

The Young Bucks, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle blended brutality with flair in a tag-team title showdown that warranted a premier spot on the card. Davis and Doyle showed off their strength throughout the match, overpowering every flashy Young Bucks comeback attempt. Superkicks and the BTE Trigger initially weren't enough, but eventually a flurry of moves provided the opening for a quick pinfall victory over Doyle.

After the match, the Motor City Machine Guns arrived in the ring to raise the Bucks' hands. The Kasper Brothers — formerly the Creed Brothers in WWE — also made their debuts, aligning with FTR to offer a post-match beatdown of the Motor City Machine Guns and the Young Bucks.

AEW already easily had the best tag-team division in wrestling, and now continues to add depth with the Kasper Brothers. A duo that never quite found their footing on the WWE main roster, the Brothers get a fresh start in AEW, where it appears they'll be thrown right into the deep end. Being presented as legit challengers alongside the likes of the Bucks, FTR and MCMG is a pretty outstanding way to arrive. Now they'll need to prove they belong.

Kazuchika Okada vs. Adam Copeland is one of those matches you just have to sign off on as part of Cope's retirement tour.

The two men's entrances popped the crowd, but I can't say Saturday's match lived up to expectations. Two of the best to do it never quite got out of first gear.

It was a match that had plenty of action, but probably would've been better served around the middle of the card rather than opening the pay-per-view. Okada used his AEW International Championship to stop a spear attempt, hit a DDT to the concrete floor, and ended Copeland's night with a Rainmaker.

It was an oddly paced match, and one that ended with a bit of a dud as Okada mocked the challenger. The rivalry would seem to continue from here, with Copeland almost certainly seeking retribution.

articles.title: UFC 334 takeaways: Ciryl Gane does it again, somehow, in his own special way
articles.summary: Ciryl Gane escapes with the UFC heavyweight title and other key takeaways from UFC 334 in Madison Square Garden.
articles.body:
UFC 334 delivered two very different types of "and still" performances in a pair of title fights. Here are the five biggest takeaways from Saturday's event in Madison Square Garden.

1. Ciryl Gane continues to put the disputed in "undisputed" UFC champ — but in such interesting ways.

First he finds a way to benefit from an egregious, career-altering eye-poke against Tom Aspinall. Then he knocks out Alex Pereira at the White House amid some complaints about illegal strikes. Now he wins a close decision over Josh Hokit with seemingly the whole of Madison Square Garden united against him . And, oh yeah, he threw in an early eye-poke there too, because why not dance with who brung ya?

But can we admit that, in the big-picture sense, Gane was just the better fighter? Josh Hokit might have been more aggressive, but what's that worth when it means marching face-first into punches for the better part of five rounds? Gane's defensive wrestling has clearly improved, and here he showed he can fight on the retreat and maintain a high pace through the championship rounds. Fans don't have to like it, but at this point maybe they do need to respect it.

2. Something tells me that's not the last time Hokit will fight for a UFC title.

It's worth remembering that he has just 11 pro MMA fights to his credit. He also didn't fight anyone who really mattered until about six months ago. That adds up to equal a man who's still a work in progress at just shy of 30 years old, so maybe we shouldn't be all that shocked if he fought like someone with more enthusiasm than sense at some points here.

It's tough sometimes to see through the persona to the athlete beneath. Hokit goes to such great lengths to present himself as a heavyweight jester that it can be hard to picture him as a potential king. But still, there's a certain diamond-in-the-rough quality here. We look at him and see what he could become if he were to put it all together. It's just that we don't know when that might happen. Though we do know it wasn't Saturday.

3. Did Kayla Harrison win that fight, or did Amanda Nunes lose it?

I'm still not sure. In the early going, Nunes seemed to be having her way. But she couldn't resist messing around with the clinch game, which gave Harrison all the opening she needed to claw her way back into it at some key moments.

It's tricky, because you don't want to deny Harrison the credit for beating the GOAT of women's MMA. But watching the fight, it felt like Nunes was right there on the verge of winning it — if only she could stay out of her own way.

Was it a consequence of all the time off since her retirement? Could this have been the dreaded ring rust (or, as the great Mauro Ranallo would say, cage corrosion)? Physically, Nunes seemed to have Harrison's number. Strategically, she was her own worst enemy.

But then maybe sometimes this sport is a battle between you and your own worst ideas. Nunes lost that battle this time.

4. Let's just be honest and admit we'll probably never see anything quite like Stephen "Wonderboy" Thompson ever again.

A karate-based fighter with an aw-shucks vibe and stubborn longevity through multiple eras of the sport? Yeah, that's not something you see every day .

Thompson broke into the UFC in 2012. At the time, it seemed almost quaint. Look at this guy doing moves out "Mighty Morphin Power Rangers" in a sport that had long since moved past the days when strip mall black belts had any chance of success.

But he made it work. And he kept making it work. Right up to this spinning heel kick victory in Madison Square Garden at the age of 43.

That's about as fairy tale an exit as anyone ever gets in this brutal, blood-and-guts world. If there's anyone who deserves it, it's probably Thompson.

5. Did anyone else catch just how weird things got at the end of that Kevin Holland vs. Uros Medic fight?

After three close rounds and one point deduction, the result was a majority draw amid scores that didn't seem to add up . Initially, the broadcast team appeared to be determined to get to the bottom of it. Then, like someone flipped a light switch, all three commentators suddenly shifted into a completely different mode and nothing more was said on the matter.

It sure felt weird as a viewer. It was jarring, like having some voice we couldn't hear (but the commentators could) directing traffic away from the thing that it made the most sense to discuss right then. It's the kind of thing that reminds you how different things are in other sports where the league doesn't control the broadcast — and why they came up with that system in the first place.

articles.title: Kayla Harrison Addresses Retirement Rumors in New Video After Win vs. Amanda Nunes at UFC 334
articles.summary: Having padded her impressive legacy with a fourth-round submission of Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Saturday, Kayla Harrison is unsure of what lies next.
articles.body:
Having padded her impressive legacy with a fourth-round submission of Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Saturday, Kayla Harrison is unsure of what lies next.

During her post-fight interview in the Octagon, Harrison said she's "got a lot of decisions to make when I get home."

The 36-year-old ran her record to 20-1 as a professional, and she's 4-0 since debuting with the UFC in 2024. Taking down Nunes is the biggest victory of her career, one that cements everything she has accomplished inside the cage.

This would be a fitting time for Harrison to walk away for good.

On top of that, getting under the bantamweight limit requires a significant effort from the champion. Harrison made her name in PFL as a lightweight, which is 20 pounds heavier than the bantamweight division.

UFC president Dana White didn't rule out staging Harrison vs. Nunes again at 145 pounds. That would presumably be more enticing for Harrison than another bantamweight title defense.

Bleacher Report's Alex Ballentine suggested Joselyne Edwards or Ailin Perez would be her next logical opponent if Harrison is willing to stay at 135 pounds. They're the No. 1 and 2 challengers in the UFC's official rankings .

Given her age and what she has achieved so far, nobody will be surprised if Harrison decides the physical cost isn't worth it anymore in the event her options are limited to another bantamweight encounter.

articles.title: Kayla ⁠⁠Harrison defeats Amanda Nunes to retain UFC bantamweight belt
articles.summary: Harrison won by a fourth-round submission against MMA legend Nunes, who made a comeback after a three-year absence.
articles.body:
Kayla ⁠⁠Harrison has retained her Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) bantamweight title with a fourth-round submission win over one of the mixed martial arts (MMA) all-time greats, Amanda Nunes, in the United States.

The American fighter leveraged her tremendous grappling skills and thwarted ⁠⁠her opponent’s attempt to take the belt back in the main event of UFC 334 at New York’s Madison Square Garden on Saturday.

A two-time Olympic judo champion, the 36-year-old Harrison was facing arguably the greatest female fighter of all time in Nunes, a dominant two-weight champion at bantamweight and featherweight before she stepped away from the sport in June 2023. But the Brazilian could not shake off the rust from her ⁠⁠⁠⁠long absence as she let the fight slip away ⁠⁠⁠⁠from her.

Nunes did well initially, looking crisp in her striking and avoiding some early takedown attempts, but she eventually succumbed to Harrison’s grappling attack, spending much of the latter part of the ⁠⁠opening two rounds on the bottom in a scarf-hold position from which she struggled to escape.

Emboldened by her ⁠⁠success, Harrison displayed the full range of her judo ⁠⁠skills with perfectly timed trips and tosses and vice-like ground control. In the fourth round, she chased Nunes down to the mat, jumping on her back and quickly sinking in a rear-naked ‌‌choke that forced the 38-year-old to submit.

“I think I’m still in shock,” said Harrison, who had surgery on herniated disks in her neck in January.

“It ‌‌feels ‌‌surreal. Sometimes I can’t believe my life. I’m just really grateful, I’m humbled, it’s an honour and a privilege to stand before you,” she said, addressing her opponent.

Harrison (20 wins, one defeat) admitted she was not sure what was next for her but took a moment to acknowledge the audience.

“New York City, I love you,” she exclaimed after the fight.

Nunes (23 wins, six defeats) took her gloves off but did not make herself available for a post-fight interview.

Meanwhile, Ciryl Gane of France defeated American Josh Hokit by unanimous decision to retain ‌‌the heavyweight title after a bruising five-round battle fought at a frenetic pace.

Gane successfully defended ‌‌his title for the first time, sweeping the scorecards 48-47, 48-47, 48-47 against Hokit.

The first round saw Gane (15 wins, two defeats) get up quickly from an early takedown by Hokit (10 wins, one defeat), then land a few sharp jabs, uppercuts and an overhand right as he countered Hokit’s forward ⁠⁠pressure. Hokit did, however, close the round with a slam with about 30 seconds remaining.

Hokit came back in the second round. After Gane stuffed an early single-leg attempt, Hokit pushed forward with determination, trading heavy right hands and clinching along the fence ⁠⁠in a very physical exchange.

Hokit carried that momentum into the third round with a scramble takedown, then worked Gane over with several clinch elbows and foot stamps before flashing him the middle finger at the bell. As Hokit’s punches began to fade in the fourth round, Gane took control, countering the challenger’s fence clinches with several body kicks, knees to the midsection and short, dirty-boxing uppercuts.

With the result still ‌‌in the balance in the fifth round, Gane stuffed Hokit’s takedown attempts and opened a cut just above his left eye, then dominated the striking with jabs, body shots and multi-punch combinations through the end of the round.

Gane kept things simple after the fight, as did the typically brash Hokit.

Hokit said he would enjoy the moment, even if he was on the receiving end.

“Resilience builds character,” Hokit said.

articles.title: Josh Hokit Hospitalized After UFC 334 Loss to Gane, 'I Saw Triple the Whole Fight.. But F--k It'
articles.summary: Josh Hokit came up short against Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 and looked the worse for wear following the fight.
articles.body:
Josh Hokit came up short against Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 and looked the worse for wear following the fight.

Hokit, who had a swollen eye, posted a video to social media saying he was still at the hospital as of 5 a.m. ET. He also suggested he "saw triple the whole fight":

Gane's 2025 fight with Tom Aspinall was ruled a no contest due to an inadvertent eye poke in the first round. It looked as though the same thing happened Saturday night with Gane catching Hokit in the left eye:

The fight obviously continued with Gane earning a unanimous decision, with the judges all scoring it 48-47. He and Hokit received the $100,000 Fight of the Night bonus.

Given how close the fighters were on the scorecards, the eye poke took on an added significance.

With his performance, Hokit managed to boost his stock in a losing effort, and he said in his post-fight interview he "will rejoice in my suffering."

"Suffering builds endurance. Endurance builds character. Character builds hope," he said. "I will never lose hope. I will be champion one day. You guys can kick me when I'm down, I'll still break your f--king leg."

The fact Hokit pushed Gane so hard despite his vision being impaired will only improve his reputation among fans.

He asked for an "immediate rematch" on social media. Should that not happen, Hokit is likely assured of getting a comparable showcase.

articles.body: Tras el Gane vs Hokit de UFC 334 (que se resolvió con un triple 48-47 para el francés), el público se ha dividido y son muchos los que alzan la voz diciendo que fue el estadounidense, y no Gane, el que venció la pelea. articles.title: From Neeraj Chopra’s Tokyo triumph to her own historic gold! How Gunjan found boxing and now eyes Olympic glory
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: For Gunjan, the road to an Olympic dream began with a newspaper feature on Neeraj Chopra.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For Gunjan, the road to an Olympic dream began with a newspaper feature on Neeraj Chopra. The Tokyo Olympics gold medallist's historic achievement inspired the Haryana teenager to believe that she, too, could represent India and win an Olympic medal. Five years later, she has taken her first major step towards that ambition, becoming the first Indian woman boxer to win gold at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar.The 17-year-old returned home with a historic gold after defeating Algeria's Bouthaina Bensalah 5-0 in the women's 48kg final. Her victory, alongside L Ambekar Meetei's gold in the men's 50kg category, helped India achieve its first-ever double gold in boxing at the Youth Olympics.Interestingly, Gunjan had not played any sport before Chopra's triumph at the Tokyo Games. And while the javelin thrower's success sparked her sporting ambition, it was boxing that eventually caught her attention."I was not playing any sport at that time. I saw Neeraj sir featured in a newspaper. That's when I thought, maybe I can do this too. I tried, and it worked out," Gunjan told PTI upon her return to Delhi.There was no elaborate thought process behind choosing boxing over other disciplines. She simply developed a liking for the sport after watching different games."There is no specific reason for that. I mean, I had watched all the games, so I don't know why I liked boxing. So I took up boxing."Parents' sacrifices, a comeback against British rivalBehind Gunjan's breakthrough has been the unwavering support of her parents, who made considerable sacrifices to ensure she could train regularly."My parents have supported me immensely. Taking me to training every day and bringing me back, morning and evening, used to get very late. Waking up early in the morning in the cold, my mother used to drop me every day, and my father used to drop me too. There is a lot of struggle by them behind me," she said.Her path to the gold medal was not without challenges. In the semifinals, Gunjan faced Great Britain's Lily Bassett, the boxer who had beaten her in the final of the World Boxing Futures Cup in Bangkok.This time, however, the Indian had a plan. Having identified Bassett's uppercut as a major threat, her coach made her work specifically on countering the punch during training."My coach made me practise a lot against the uppercut, and because of that, it did not have much effect this time," she said.Gunjan won the semifinal 4-1 before producing a dominant performance against Bensalah in the final, with all five judges scoring the bout in her favour."There was some pressure beforehand, but not during the bout. During the bout, I just thought that I had to give my best," she said.The Class 12 student, who is pursuing Arts, also manages to balance academics with her demanding training schedule."As for studies and sports, well, when exams come around, I study, take the exams, and pass," she said.Asian Games, Commonwealth Games and Olympics nextHaving made her mark at the youth level, Gunjan is already looking ahead to the senior category, which she will enter after a year. Her ambitions now extend to the Asian Games, Commonwealth Games and, ultimately, the Olympics."Right now, I have thought about the senior category, because after one year I will move up to seniors. I have planned for the Asian Games, Commonwealth Games and Olympics," she said.For Gunjan, though, the journey from being inspired by Chopra's Olympic gold to winning a historic Youth Olympic title is only the beginning. The teenager now has her sights firmly set on the biggest prize of all.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jon Jones Appears to Troll Josh Hokit After Ciryl Gane's Win at UFC 334
articles.summary: Former UFC heavyweight champion Jon Jones appeared to enjoy watching Josh Hokit lose to current titleholder Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 on Saturday.
articles.body:
Former UFC heavyweight champion Jon Jones appeared to enjoy watching Josh Hokit lose to current titleholder Ciryl Gane in the main event of UFC 334 on Saturday.

Despite training at the same gym as Hokit, Jones posted an Instagram video trolling him while the result of the fight was announced, with Gane winning by unanimous decision.

"Same coaches, different results," Jones wrote in the caption , referencing their shared trainers, Greg Jackson and Mike Winkeljohn. As he watched the fight result, he said in the video, "Put your hand down [Hokit]. Good job, Frenchman!"

Jones claimed the heavyweight title in 2023 by defeating Gane via first-round submission. He referenced Hokit in more social media posts, noting that the challenger bad-mouthed him before his loss:

Presumably, Jackson and Winkeljohn would've had the blueprint to give Hokit the chance to defeat Gane again, but things didn't play out that way on Saturday night. Despite his relentless pressure in the early rounds, Hokit failed to put Gane away, and the defending champ stepped on the gas in the final two rounds to secure the win.

Jones retired last year, so there likely won't be any in-fighting at the gym between him and Hokit. The 29-year-old will have to go back to the drawing board as he tries to earn another shot at the heavyweight title.

articles.title: Alex Pereira respects Josh Hokit after UFC 334 ‘robbery’ — ‘I thought he won for sure’
articles.summary: Josh Hokit is very good at making people hate him during fight weeks, but also very good at creating fans on fight night. That’s what happened with Alex Pere...
articles.body:
Josh Hokit is very good at making people hate him during fight weeks, but also very good at creating fans on fight night. That's what happened with Alex Pereira, who has previously called Hokit a disrespectful r—ard. After seeing "The Incredible Hok" almost take the belt off Ciryl Gane at UFC 334, though? Pereira now has a lot of respect for the man.

Gane beat Hokit via 48-47 unanimous decision (see the scorecards here), and Pereira made it clear he felt the judges got it very wrong.

"Call the police! Call the police!" he said on an Instagram post. "Hello, can you come down to Madison Square Garden? Yeah, there's a robbery happening right now."

"I thought it was a robbery, man," Pereira said backstage following the fight. "I thought Hokit won the fight, for sure. Gane didn't do anything. I wanted Gane to win, but come on. Not like that. That's a bit much, right? Unless I was watching a different fight, man. Really? That's crazy."

Pereira even sought out Hokit to congratulate him on his performance.

"Bro, he says for him, you won, bro," Pereira's translator told Hokit. "So he respects."

We'll see whether that respect survives Hokit's endless trash talk and what feels like an inevitable clash between the two heavyweights. Leading up to UFC 334, Dana White repeatedly said a fight between Hokit and Pereira would be massive. For now, though, Pereira has to get through his fight with Sergei Pavlovich at UFC 335 first.

articles.title: Josh Hokit releases statement following UFC 334 title fight loss to Ciryl Gane
articles.summary: Josh Hokit wants another piece of Ciryl Gane after UFC 334 title fight
articles.body:
Josh Hokit isn't taking his UFC 334 loss lying down.

"The Incredible Hok" fought tooth and nail against heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane the main event at Madison Square Garden in New York, but fell short on the scorecards despite a gutsy effort. Shortly after the conclusion of Saturday's show, Hokit hopped onto to call for another crack at Gane.

And he wants it as soon as possible. See Hokit's post below:

"Immediate rematch," Hokit wrote. "Please."

After the fight, Gane and Hokit showed each other respect, and Hokit went away from his usual volatile post-fight promo style to simply say that the loss will make him stronger. It was Hokit's first defeat following a 10-0 start to his pro MMA career.

While the UFC 334 main event was unquestionably a crowdpleaser, there are other notable heavyweights waiting in the wings for their shot at Gane. Tom Aspinall—the man who vacated the undisputed title due to eye injuries suffered in a fight with Gane in October 2025—will presumably get the first crack if he's able to return in early 2027, and Alexander Volkov has made a strong case by winning three straight fights to bounce back from a controversial decision loss to Gane.

Gane's next opponent could also come from the UFC 335 co-main event, which sees Sergei Pavlovich take on Alex Pereira, the man Gane defeated at UFC White House to become interim champion this past June.

articles.title: 'Free Money,' Kayla Harrison Names Ronda Rousey for Dream Fight After UFC 334 Win vs. Amanda Nunes
articles.summary: After defeating Amanda Nunes in the co-main event of UFC 334 on Saturday night, bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has her eyes set on another legend.
articles.body:
After defeating Amanda Nunes in the co-main event of UFC 334 on Saturday night, bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has her eyes set on another legend.

When asked if she has a dream opponent for her next outing, Harrison named former UFC star and her former judo training partner, Ronda Rousey.

"If Ronda wants to come get some," Harrison said (h/t Alexander K. Lee of MMA Fighting). "Could be fun. Free money."

Rousey returned to MMA in May after nine-plus years away from the sport, defeating Gina Carano in the main event of MVP's inaugural MMA card on Netflix. She declared that her return was a one-off, but that didn't stop her from taking shots at Harrison and the UFC.

While a fight between Rousey and Harrison appears to be a long shot, Harrison's days at 135 pounds could already be over. After she defended her title by submitting Nunes in the fourth round, she was told that UFC CEO Dana White was open to a rematch with a featherweight championship on the line, and she welcomed the idea.

"Uh, 145?" she said for her preference over another bantamweight defense. "I've got to go get that other belt."

articles.title: Johnny Fisher wants to fight Kristian Prenga, the man who almost derailed Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua, early next year
articles.summary: Kristian Prenga almost knocked out Anthony Joshua in his tune up fight before Tyson Fury; Johnny Fisher now wants to test himself against Prenga early in 2027; Watch Aaron McKenna vs Jevgenijs Aleksejevs on Friday December 4 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
In July, Prenga boxed Joshua in what was meant to be a tune-up fight for the former world champion. Instead Prenga put him down heavily twice in their first round. He was on the edge of victory only for Joshua to storm back and knock him out in the second round.

Prenga caught the eye of the boxing world in that fight and Fisher would like the man who almost beat Joshua to be his next opponent.

"Prenga would be good. That's a good sort of stepping stone to where I want to be. Someone who's fought one of the best heavyweights we've had in Great Britain in recent years, or in memory in general," Fisher told Sky Sports .

"So to be in the ring with someone like that, who carries knockout power, carries the ability to drop people, like Anthony Joshua, at the top of the division - so let's see what I can do."

Fisher added: "He almost did [beat AJ]. That's the fine margins of professional heavyweight boxing and there's jeopardy in it, I said that in the build up to the last one . It definitely is exciting."

Fisher wants to box early next year, even though his last fight, against Michael Pirotton in September, turned into a gruelling battle.

"We're looking at February time," he said. "It'll be here before you know it. I want to start my camp on January 1. I want to build some good foundations.

" Dillian Whyte has been thrown in the hat , but maybe that's something for a summer showdown if I come through another test before then."

He has every intention of improving on that last performance. "I felt like I'd been through the mill a little bit, it was a tough, tough fight. Credit to Pirotton, he was a tough operator. I knew it was going to be," Fisher said.

"When he gave me a death stare I knew this was his World Cup final. He's a tough man, never been stopped and I boxed very well in the first four rounds and just that second wind never came. That was to do with things we can adjust and make better."

Fisher did sting Pirotton in the 10th and final round. "I don't know where I found that energy in the last round but I've dug deep before to get to the final bell and I know I've always got that in me. But I don't want to always rely on it every time," he said.

"Me and Tony [Sims, his trainer] are still gelling, there's things that we can change in the camp.

"I couldn't have trained any harder but it didn't look that way because I probably left a tiny bit in that last week.

"That's why it's exciting as well," he added, "because we still haven't seen the best version of me."

articles.title: Cardiff's Kronk? The gym where Welsh champions train
articles.summary: Under the stewardship of former middleweight champion Gary Lockett, the Phoenix club has become a home for Welsh boxing excellence.
articles.body:
In the red corner, a two-time world champion staying sharp as he waits for his return.

His opponents, a succession of boxers readying themselves for an undercard bout that could be a key step in their careers.

And out the back, the fancy dress climax to a Halloween boxing camp for local kids that mixed the sweet science with arts and crafts.

Welcome to Llanrumney Phoenix ABC, situated on the eastern edge of Cardiff as the suburbs rise up and away from the city centre of the Welsh capital.

Barrett stops Gwynne for vacant lightweight title

Adames beats Welshman Warburton by unanimous decision

Cordina unlikely to fight Pacquiao on Joshua-Fury card

It is both six kilometres and a million miles away from the bright lights of the Principality Stadium, the focus of the boxing world on 11 December when it stages the heavyweight showdown between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury.

But it is also the place where the steps towards it are made.

Some are further along than others, such as Joe Cordina, whose image complete with world title straps is one of several champions that hang high above the main sparring ring, flanked by a plethora of punchbags.

Or former featherweight champ Lee Selby, now a bareknuckle boxer but lending his experience to the sparring as Gavin Gwynne gets ready for his own battle with Zelfa Barrett, a bout that would ultimately end in a fifth-round stoppage for the Welshman.

Then there are those of the next generation, priming themselves for a primetime audience with this week's BBC-broadcast show on the undercard of Lauren Price's title defence against Michaela Kotaskova at Cardiff's Utilita Arena, the exciting pair of Brandon Scott and Rhys Edwards included.

The closeness of the fight night and the amount of fighters creates a tangible buzz between the buzzes of the timer that pings into life every three minutes. Words of advice and tips from their own fights won – and lost – are shared between rounds, between the jokes at each others' expense.

Eleven pros throwing countless punches, all adding up to the sense this is one of the centres of the Welsh boxing world. Cardiff's Kronk, , external if you like.

"You've got every level here, from former world champions to guys who dream about that, British title level, prospects – but everyone is treated the same," says Brandon Scott, who has recently returned closer to home following a spell training in Sheffield.

"I had a trial and trained with the boys and it felt I'd been here for years. I was asking Gary to please train me the next day."

Gary is Gary Lockett, the former middleweight world title challenger, recently inducted into the British Boxing Hall of Fame and who has coached since hanging up his gloves in 2008.

"I came here in 2018," says Lockett, who accepted an invite that year from the club's founder and proud local, Tony Richards, to set up camp in the gym that doubles as a community hub in one of the more deprived areas of the city.

As well as running classes for aspiring young amateur boxers, it has won recognition for inclusion activities and the support it offers.

"We obviously have our guys training for their fights, but we're also part of this community. That's important," Lockett says.

"We're not Premier League footballers who are on a different planet to most people.

"And we make sure there's no bad eggs here. We want them to be good people first and foremost, as well as good boxers.

"My first aim is always to educate to be the right kind of person out of the ring."

Live on BBC Two Wales and iPlayer from 21:00 GMT

That is obvious. But it's also clear that it's what could be earned inside the ring that inspires the electricity in the air this October morning.

The thought of a sell-out fight night in the city looms large, with Price's rising tide as a boxing star helping to lift Lockett's stable in terms of opportunities.

"I like to think of Cardiff as a fight town, but we do struggle in Wales with the big promoters coming here," says Lockett, who also manages around 20 fighters, including the Enzo Maccarinelli-trained Willy Gilheaney and Josh Kelly who will also appear on the Price undercard.

"It's very hard to build these guys on small-hall bills, so we need platforms like this. They know they need to take the opportunity, sell as many tickets as you can, because this could be your shop window and the chance to be signed by a big promoter."

'Spiderman' Scott swinging back into action

Swansea's Scott has had the experience of that, earning an early-career deal with promoter Eddie Hearn's Matchroom.

Injuries and some personal issues saw him take time away before – fittingly – arriving at the Phoenix under Lockett.

"Everything is back to normal," says the 23-year-old, who next faces journeyman Mexican Erik Omar Lopez.

"I had a lot at a young age and perhaps I needed a bit of time to mature, and now mentally and physically I'm in the right place.

"I feel like I'm starting my career over again and, coming here, I've giving myself the best chance to go again."

The boxer with a Spiderman tattoo and who calls himself the "baddest nerd on the planet" says he is "still a silly goose" but Lockett says he is learning more and more, including an "eye-opening" time training in Japan.

His sparring session with Edwards is fascinating, several fighters taking a break from their own workouts to offer tips as the similarly styled featherweights enjoy the endurance test.

In fact, a smile never seems to be off the face of Edwards, whose fight with former world bantamweight title challenger Lee McGregor serves as the main support act to Price's headlining bout.

"I'll probably sell 30 tickets before leaving the house," laughs the 26-year-old, one of 11 siblings from Penygraig who previously admitted to sleeping in the Llanrumney gym close to fights to avoid the chaos at home.

Not afraid of social media - a TikTok of him dodging shots in a pillow fight hit more than 10m views a few years back - and admitting to feeling like a minor celebrity such is the extent of the support he gets from his valleys hometown, Edwards is aware of the serious business fast approaching as he puts in the work.

Having recovered from a first professional defeat in December 2024 – losing on points to Peter McGrail after taking the Riyadh fight with four days' notice – he missed out on a chance of a British title in a draw with Gully Powar in Cardiff in April.

"It's kind of make or break – anything less than a win will push me back a year or two," Edwards says. "A big win sets me up, so the stakes are high."

As is the opportunity, something the Llanrumney gym is all too aware of as the hits come and the hard work continues.

And all hope that it leads to something more down the road where the bright lights beckon and championship fights call.

But it all begins in places like Llanrumney.

articles.title: Paddy Pimblett: "Me encantaría mandar a Ilia Topuria a la jubilación"
articles.standfirst: El inglés vuelve a cargar contra 'El Matador'
articles.summary: El inglés vuelve a cargar contra 'El Matador'
articles.body: Si hace unos días Paddy Pimblett aprovechaba una entrevista en el podcast de Joe Rogan para atacar a Ilia Topuria... ahora ha sido otra charla en 'Talksports' la que ha servido al de Liverpool de plataforma para volver a 'cargar' contra el 'Matador'. Un asedio constante que tiene como finalidad convencer a la UFC de organizar el que sería uno de los combates más 'calientes' de los últimos tiempos. Paddy, que finalizó en el pasado mes de julio a Saint-Denis por sumisión antes del minuto de combate, sabe que vuelve a estar de actualidad. Se quedó a las puertas del interinato en el peso ligero (perdió ante Gaethje), pero vuelve a buscar el camino al cinturón. Y ese sendero puede estar bloqueado por Topuria... o que el hispanogeorgiano sea el mismo destino final. Depende del futuro de Gaethje. "La división está un poco revuelta ahora mismo porque, obviamente, Justin tiene el cinturón, pero nadie sabe qué va a hacer: si va a pelear o si se va a retirar, así que tenemos que ver qué hace", analizaba el propio Paddy. Y es que si Gaethje no pelea, el título quedaría vacante... con Topuria, Tsarukyan y el propio Paddy aspirando a esa corona... sin contar con un Charles Oliveira que defiende este mes de diciembre su título del BMF ante Diego Lopes. Una victoria 'catapultaría' a 'Do Bronx'. Pero Paddy, está claro, quiere a Topuria: "Todo el mundo quiere verme pelear contra él. Me encantaría pelear contra Ilia. Es decir, me encantaría mandarlo a la jubilación". Un reto directo al doble campeón de la UFC.

articles.title: La hora de Aleksandre Topuria
articles.standfirst: 'El Conquistador' pelea este fin de semana en Qatar ante Santiago Luna
articles.summary: 'El Conquistador' pelea este fin de semana en Qatar ante Santiago Luna
articles.body: Es semana de Aleksandre Topuria (7-1) en UFC. Y eso no es decir poca cosa. 'El Conquistador', hermano mayor de Ilia Topuria, se enfrentará este sábado en Qatar al mexicano Santiago Luna (8-1) en el combate que cierra las preliminares de un eventazo en Doha. Será la tercera pelea del hispanogeorgiano en la mejor liga de MMA del mundo... con un impoluto récord de 2-0 (dos victorias) hasta la fecha. La expectativa siempre es máxima en torno a Aleksandre. Por lo poco que se le ha visto (dos peleas en UFC, ambas con 15 minutos completos dentro de la jaula) y por lo que se espera que pueda llegar a lograr. Los elogios siempre han sido grandes de parte de los que han entrenado con él (el propio Ilia, Merab Dvalishvili...) y ser el entrenador 'jefe' de un doblecampeón no es poca cosa. Ahora, tras vencer a Thicknesse y Almakhan en su primer año en UFC, Aleksandre vuelve un año después al mismo sitio de su último duelo: Doha. Se enfrentará al mexicano Santiago Luna en el combate que cierra las preliminares, sobre las 18.30 hora española. Aleksandre, que lleva ya más de una semana en Qatar junto a su hermano Ilia, parte en las casas de apuestas como muy favorito. Y sin embargo, es un combate que promete ser complicado para el hispanogeorgiano. No por demérito de 'Aleks, que ha demostrado muchas de sus cualidades en sus dos primeros combates en UFC, sino porque 'Borderboy' es un rival peligroso. Luna, que entrena en California, irrumpió en la UFC con dos victorias que lo colocaron en la órbita de los aficionados: una finalización ante Quang Le y un triunfo por decisión unánime contra Ángel Pacheco. Sin embargo, viene de perder: Bryce Mitchell, ex rival de Ilia Topuria, lo sometió en junio. Aleksandre, mientras, buscará su primera finalización en UFC, algo que le ha sido esquivo ante Thicknesse y Almakhan en sus combates anteriores.

articles.title: Chris Eubank Jr vs Kell Brook: British rivals are holding talks for a blockbuster battle but terms are yet to be agreed
articles.summary: Chris Eubank Jr is considering options for a return to the ring , including a potential showdown with Kell Brook; talks are ongoing for Eubank Jr vs Brook but terms are yet to be agreed; former IBF welterweight champion Brook has not fought since he defeated Amir Khan in February 2022;
articles.body:
Eubank Jr is considering options for a return to the ring and a showdown with Brook, the former IBF world welterweight champion, has emerged as a potential fight.

But Elliott Amoakoh, executive director of Eubank Jr's management team, Nova Sport LLC, has told Sky Sports that terms have not yet been agreed.

"Talks are ongoing but the date, purse and location are yet to be confirmed," Amoakoh told Sky Sports.

Brook has been absent from the ring since he settled his long-running rivalry with Amir Khan in February 2022, winning the grudge fight with a sixth-round stoppage.

In the aftermath of that win, Brook was linked with a fight against Eubank, although nothing materialised and the Sheffield man entered retirement.

Eubank Jr switched his attention to domestic clashes with Liam Smith, defeating the Liverpudlian emphatically in a rematch.

He beat Conor Benn on points in April 2025, then lost the return bout on the scorecards last November in his most recent fight.

Brook had been due to have a comeback fight in Dubai in March, but the event did not go ahead as planned and he is now in negotiations over resuming his boxing career against Eubank Jr.
